subject: Reasoning
description: Clock problems — angle between hands, time when hands coincide / are perpendicular / opposite, mirror image, gain/loss in time.

questions.stem: What is the angle between the HOUR and MINUTE hands at 3:15?
questions.explanation: FORMULA for ANGLE between hands: |30H − 5.5M|, where H = hour, M = minute. Plug H=3, M=15: |30(3) − 5.5(15)| = |90 − 82.5| = 7.5°. KEY DERIVATION: (1) HOUR HAND moves 30°/hour = 0.5°/minute. (2) MINUTE HAND moves 360°/hour = 6°/minute. (3) RELATIVE speed = 6 − 0.5 = 5.5°/minute. At time H:M, hour hand has moved 30H + 0.5M; minute hand 6M; difference = 30H + 0.5M − 6M = 30H − 5.5M (could be negative — take absolute value). EXAMPLE 3:15: hour hand at 90° + 7.5° = 97.5°; minute hand at 90°. Difference = 7.5°. KEY VALUES (memorize): (1) 12:00 — 0° (overlap). (2) 3:00 — 90°. (3) 6:00 — 180° (opposite). (4) 9:00 — 270° (= 90° on other side). (5) 12:30 — 165°. CIRCLE = 360°; full minute = 6°; full hour = 30°. CLOCK BONUS facts: hands coincide 11 times in 12 hours (~once every 65.45 min — actually 65 5/11 min). Hands are at 90° → 22 times in 12 hours. 180° → 11 times in 12 hours. PYQ FREQUENCY: clock-angle problems in SSC CGL Tier 1, IBPS Clerk, RRB NTPC — 1× per paper.

questions.stem: How many times in a DAY do the hour and minute hands of a clock COINCIDE (overlap)?
questions.explanation: In 12 HOURS, hour and minute hands COINCIDE 11 TIMES (NOT 12, despite intuition). REASON: minute hand 'gains' 360° on hour hand every 12/11 hours = ~65.45 min; first coincidence after 12:00 is at ~1:05:27 (12/11 hr). They coincide at: 12:00, 1:05:27, 2:10:54, 3:16:21, 4:21:49, 5:27:16, 6:32:43, 7:38:10, 8:43:38, 9:49:05, 10:54:32 — and then 12:00 again (the 11th). NEVER at exactly 11 (because the next coincidence after 10:54:32 IS the 12:00 mark). In 24 HOURS: 11 × 2 = 22 times. PARALLEL: Hands at 180° (OPPOSITE): also 11 times in 12 hr; 22 times in 24 hr. Hands at 90° (RIGHT ANGLE): 22 times in 12 hr; 44 times in 24 hr. KEY METHOD: relative motion approach. Minute hand catches up to hour hand at 5.5°/min; gap closes 360° in 360/5.5 = 65.45 min ≈ 12/11 hr. PYQ FREQUENCY: clock 'coincide / opposite / right angle' counts in SSC CGL Tier 2, IBPS Clerk Pre, RRB NTPC 1× per paper.

questions.stem: At what time between 5 and 6 o'clock will the two hands of a clock be at RIGHT ANGLE (90°)?
questions.explanation: Apply ANGLE FORMULA: |30H − 5.5M| = 90°. At H=5: |150 − 5.5M| = 90. CASE 1: 150 − 5.5M = 90 → 5.5M = 60 → M = 60/5.5 = 120/11 ≈ 10.909 min. So 5:10:54.5 (10 min, 54.5 sec). CASE 2: 5.5M − 150 = 90 → 5.5M = 240 → M = 240/5.5 = 480/11 ≈ 43.636 min. So 5:43:38.2. So between 5 and 6 the hands are at 90° AT TWO TIMES. GENERAL: in any 12-hour period, hands are at 90° → 22 times (≈ once every ~32 minutes). KEY METHOD: |30H − 5.5M| = θ has TWO solutions in [0, 60) (when both H and θ are fixed). Verify each is in valid minute range. CLOCK PROBLEM TYPES: (1) ANGLE = 0° (coincide). (2) ANGLE = 90° (right angle). (3) ANGLE = 180° (opposite). (4) ANGLE = θ° (any specific angle). (5) MIRROR-IMAGE problems — clock mirror. (6) TIME GAINING/LOSING — clock running fast/slow. (7) BROKEN CLOCK — second hand frozen but hour and minute hands work. PYQ FREQUENCY: clock-angle word problems in SSC CGL Tier 2, IBPS PO Mains 1× per paper. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests algebraic precision + clock-mechanics intuition.

questions.stem: A clock GAINS 5 minutes every hour. If set correctly at 12 noon, what time does it show at 12 noon next day (24 hours actual)?
questions.explanation: GAINS 5 min/hour means the clock RUNS FAST — every actual hour, it shows 65 minutes. In 24 ACTUAL HOURS, total gain = 5 × 24 = 120 minutes = 2 hours. Clock shows 12:00 PM + 2 hours = 2:00 PM. KEY: 'gains' = clock's apparent time RUNS AHEAD of true time. 'Loses' = clock's time falls BEHIND. CALCULATION FORMULA: actual gain (or loss) = (rate per hour) × (actual hours elapsed). PRACTICE: (1) Clock loses 3 min/hour; after 5 actual hours = 15 min slow. (2) Clock gains 1 min/day; after 30 days = 30 min ahead. (3) 2 clocks: A gains 2 min/hour, B loses 1 min/hour; after how long they show 1 hour difference? (Combined drift = 3 min/hour; need 60 min difference; 60/3 = 20 hours). VARIANT problems: 'A clock gains uniformly, was set right at 8 AM Monday; at 9 PM Tuesday it showed 9:25 PM. When was it correct?' — calculate the rate, work back. CLOCK MECHANICAL ERROR: real mechanical clocks gain or lose ~1 sec/day; quartz clocks ~1 sec/year; atomic clocks ~1 sec/300 million years. PYQ FREQUENCY: gain-loss in time problems in SSC CGL Tier 1, IBPS Clerk Pre 1× per paper.

questions.stem: What is the angle traced by the HOUR HAND of a clock in 4 hours and 30 minutes?
questions.explanation: HOUR HAND moves 360° in 12 hours → 30° per hour → 0.5° per minute. In 4 hr 30 min = 4.5 hours = 270 min: angle = 4.5 × 30° = 135° (or 270 × 0.5° = 135°). KEY HOUR-HAND speeds: (1) 30°/hour. (2) 0.5°/min. (3) 1/120°/sec. KEY MINUTE-HAND speeds: (1) 360°/hour. (2) 6°/min. (3) 0.1°/sec. SECOND HAND speeds: (1) 360°/min. (2) 6°/sec. PRACTICE: (1) Hour hand in 90 min = 90 × 0.5° = 45°. (2) Minute hand in 25 min = 25 × 6° = 150°. (3) Second hand in 12 sec = 12 × 6° = 72°. (4) Hour hand in 7 hours = 7 × 30 = 210° (or equivalently, −150° measured short way). KEY VARIATION: ANGLE BETWEEN HANDS at any time uses |30H − 5.5M|. Avoid confusing 'angle traced by single hand' (just speed × time) with 'angle between two hands' (relative). PRACTICE: 'How many times do hour and minute hands form 60° between 9 and 10 o'clock?' — twice (once before they overlap at ~9:49, once after). PYQ FREQUENCY: hand-angle calculation in SSC CGL, IBPS, RRB 1× per paper.

questions.stem: What is the MIRROR IMAGE of a clock showing 4:20?
questions.explanation: MIRROR IMAGE OF CLOCK formula: subtract the time from 11:60 (or 12:00 conceptually). Plug 4:20: mirror = 11:60 − 4:20 = 7:40. EXPLANATION: when you look at a clock in a mirror, LEFT-RIGHT reverses. The time T's mirror is computed as: 12:00 − T (with hours and minutes correctly reflected). Equivalent: 11:60 − T (since 12:00 = 11:60). FORMULA: if time is H:M, mirror = (11 − H):(60 − M), with adjustments. PRACTICE: (1) 3:00 → 9:00. (2) 6:30 → 5:30. (3) 9:15 → 2:45. (4) 12:00 → 12:00. (5) 8:50 → 3:10. KEY ADJUSTMENTS: when M = 0, mirror is (12 − H):00. So 6:00 → 6:00 (palindromic). 4:00 → 8:00. RELATED: WATER REFLECTION of clock — UP-DOWN flip; different from mirror. Computing water reflection: 6:00 − T (with adjustments). EXAM TIP: visualize the clock face flipped horizontally. The numerals' positions: 12 stays, 6 stays; 1↔11, 2↔10, 3↔9, 4↔8, 5↔7. PYQ FREQUENCY: clock-mirror in SSC CGL Tier 1, IBPS Clerk 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: An accurate clock shows 8 o'clock in the morning. Through how many degrees does the HOUR HAND rotate when the clock shows 2 o'clock in the afternoon?
questions.explanation: Time elapsed from 8 AM to 2 PM = 6 HOURS. Hour hand moves 30°/hour. Total rotation = 6 × 30 = 180°. ANSWER: 180°. KEY: simple multiplication, but careful about: (1) 12-hour vs 24-hour clock (here 8 AM to 2 PM is 6 hours, not 18 hours — only one cycle on the clock). (2) Direction: clockwise (hour hand goes around clockwise on standard analog clock). PRACTICE — INDIA UPSC analytical-reasoning style: 'Through how many degrees does the SECOND HAND rotate in 1 minute?' = 360°. 'Through how many degrees does the MINUTE HAND rotate from 9:00 AM to 12:30 PM?' = 3.5 hr × 360° = 1260° (multiple full rotations). 'How many TIMES does the second hand revolve around the clock from 6:00 to 6:45?' = 45 (one revolution per minute). EXAM TIP — 12-HOUR cycle math: hour hand rotates fully every 12 hours = 360°. So in T hours, it rotates 30 × T degrees (mod 360). For UPSC analytical reasoning: clock + calendar problems blend; e.g., 'on Monday at 10 AM clock shows correct time; it loses 5 min/day; on Friday at 2 PM what does it show?' — calculate days+hours, multiply rate. PYQ FREQUENCY: clock-rotation in SSC CGL, RRB NTPC, UPSC CSAT — 1× per paper.
